prompt: Write the function tokenize(text) in /work/lexer.py. It returns a list of (kind, value) tuples, where value is the exact source text of the token. Each token is the longest match at its position. The token kinds: NUM is one or more digits, optionally followed by a '.' and one or more digits (12, 3.75); NAME is a letter or '_' followed by any letters, digits or '_'; OP is one of ** + - * / ( ), where two adjacent '*' are one '**' token. Digits are ASCII 0-9 and letters are ASCII a-z and A-Z only. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate tokens and give no token. Any other character, including a '.' that is not part of a NUM, raises ValueError. There are no signed numbers: '-3' is OP '-' and then NUM '3'. The visible tests are run with: python3 -m pytest -q test_lexer.py
